$comment: The site's own facts, as data: which pack is the ground, which mode a reader
who has never chosen gets, and the set of sites the family's menu moves between.
A pack identifier is a token, and this file is the one place this site picks one,
so a renamed or retired pack is a compile error rather than a mark that quietly
inherits the ground. A mark and a ground are two different axes: the ground is
stable for the life of the page and comes from `ground` below, and a product's
mark comes from its own entry in `products`.
Two renames are recorded here rather than in prose. The first line called this
pack rose and the design system called it blush. Then the family's map asked for
a gold ground for this product, and the token build grew one, so the ground moved
from blush to gold and Prism's mark in the directory went the other way: Prism
carries no pack at all now, which is the one case `ProductMark` draws as the full
spectrum, because the design system itself owns every hue. `rose` and `blush` are
not this site's identifiers any more, and a mark carrying one would either match
nothing or paint somebody else's colour while claiming this product's.
**Every `href` here is absolute, including this site's own.** It was `/` until the
bar's family arrived as a menu, and that was a defect the old switcher hid rather
than caused: the old switcher drew only the siblings, so this entry was never read
by the one control that uses it. A menu of destinations that leave this site is
rendered with `target="_blank"` on every row, and `/` in a new tab is a new tab on
the page the reader is already on. The five sites are five origins and the file
now says so. `test/site-chrome.test.tsx` is what holds it: it reads the rendered
set rather than the JSON, so a relative href is a finding on the page and not a
reading of this comment.
